context_length: Single sequence in this benchmark; E1 can also take retrieved homologs as context
summary: The 600M Profluent E1 encoder: the largest released E1 model, used here on single sequences to produce 1280-dim embeddings.
architecture: Encoder-only transformer, 30 layers and hidden size 1280, with attention within each sequence and a global layer across sequences every third layer. Run here on single sequences.
pretraining_data: About 4 trillion tokens from the Profluent Protein Atlas.
pretraining_objective: Masked language modeling with retrieved homologous sequences in the context, read through block-causal multi-sequence attention; the released models also run on a single sequence.
key_innovations: Largest released E1 model (the family has 150M, 300M and 600M), with retrieval-augmented conditioning on homologs
Reported state-of-the-art zero-shot fitness and unsupervised contact prediction
when_to_use: As a larger modern ESM-style encoder (1280-dim); its retrieval augmentation is not used here, since the benchmark embeds single sequences.
caveats: 2025 preprint. It was designed to condition on retrieved homologs, which this benchmark does not supply. Weights under the Profluent-E1 license, which allows research and commercial use with attribution.

citations.authors: Jain, S., Beazer, J., Ruffolo, J. A., Bhatnagar, A., Madani, A.
citations.title: E1: Retrieval-Augmented Protein Encoder Models
